descripcion: At B2 speculation is expressed with the most common modal verbs: might, could, will probably. The full speculation chain with a grounding observation and an acknowledged limit (C1) isn't the focus yet — a clearly graded prediction is enough.

ejemplos.texto: It might rain later, so bring a jacket.
This will probably take longer than expected.
It's bound to change again before the end of the year.

notas: Might and could are close in meaning here and both express a real but uncertain possibility.
Probably goes between the subject and the main verb: it will probably happen, not it probably will happen (though both are heard).
Bound to is a strong prediction, close to certain — use it only when you really mean it.

contraste.es: Spanish predicts with the future or the future of probability (será que…), which can lead to overusing will and avoiding might or could, losing the lower degree of certainty.
contraste.de: German könnte maps well onto could or might, and wird wohl onto will probably. The scale of certainty therefore transfers directly.
contraste.it: The Italian future of probability (sarà a casa) tends to become he will be at home, which sounds more certain than intended. Potrebbe maps well onto might or could.
contraste.fr: Il se peut que corresponds to might and il pourrait to could, so the lower degrees of certainty transfer well. The French future maps onto will for firm predictions.
contraste.pt: Pode ser que corresponds to might, and vai + infinitive to going to. The scale of certainty therefore transfers well.

errores: Using only will for every prediction, regardless of certainty.
Using bound to for something that's actually uncertain.

traducciones.de: Es besteht eine gute Chance, dass…
traducciones.fr: Il y a de fortes chances que…

autochequeo: Have I used more than one modal verb, not just will every time?
Is probably in the right position in the sentence?
Does the level of certainty match how sure I actually am?
Have I used bound to only when genuinely confident?
Are might and could used interchangeably where appropriate?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the modal verbs used for prediction. Check the position of probably and whether the certainty level fits the context. Do not rewrite the text.
